children.text: This lesson is intended for use in sophomore level high school classrooms, though it could certainly be adapted for other grade levels in 9-12 education. It serves as an introduction to working with sound in poetry, moving students through the analytical process of close reading a poem (paraphrase → observe → contextualize → analyze → argue → reflect).
By the end of the ~50 minute lesson,
students will practice applying poetic analysis of sound to their own poem of choice from around the world, culminating in an informal oral analysis.
Students can work individually or in pairs. It is entirely self-paced for the students. To deliver this lesson, simply provide this project link to students:

They will navigate through the lesson by reading, watching, and listening to the resources in the project. Anything that is bolded is an action item for students to read/watch/do; anything that's bolded and underlined is a question (or questions) that students will respond to in a method of your choosing (e.g., Google Doc, notebook paper, etc.).
